title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: The Claim Record of a Cover Over Its Life
content:
Over the life of a delivered shipment, more than one claim may come to rest on the same cover of `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`. This page describes how the cover's record moves as claims on it are decided and succeed one another, and which party performs each kind of act.

## Scope

The account applies to any cargo cover on which one claim is followed by another. When every claim that has been open on such a cover is decided and closed, the record shows the cover at closed claim with no claim open; each approval has raised the cover's balance of approved settlements awaiting payment by its sum, and each rejection stands with its controlled reason at 0.00. A notice that meets none of the grounds settled at registration remains an open claim while its documents are gathered.

## The parties

Decisions on claims, whether approvals of settlement or rejections, are taken by the desk, and the desk closes decided claims on the cover. Lodging a notice of loss is the claimant's own act; the desk never lodges one for the claimant.

## How each kind of act bears on the cover's record

- **Closing.** Closing applies to a claim that carries a decision. An approval entry booked on a claim is such a decision, and so is a rejection entry; whichever of the two stands on a claim, that claim is decided.
- **Deciding.** An approval of settlement, and a rejection alike, can be booked only while the cover shows the claim concerned as its open claim. A rejection decides the particular claim file it names.
- **Lodging.** A notice opens a claim, and a cover carries one open claim at a time; a notice opens its claim on a cover standing at active or at closed claim.
- **Timing.** None of these acts waits on anything outside the line's own records. No survey, document, payment or lapse of time stands between them; each takes effect on the records the moment it is booked.
